description: MonkeyMode guardrail preset: Godot 4 (GDScript; C# files are covered by the Unity-style C# rules only if you add them). Applies to scripts under scopeRoot. GDScript uses # comments, which the comment detector does not see, so noComments stays false. Checked against the Godot 4.7 docs.

rules.message: Reaching up the tree with ../ node paths is banned. The script then depends on where its scene is instanced, and breaks silently when a scene is reparented. Export a typed reference (@export var target: Node3D), use a %UniqueName inside the same scene, or let the parent wire children up. See docs/engine/guardrails.md

Absolute /root/ node paths are banned. They hard-code the scene tree layout and fail whenever load order or autoload names change. Use an autoload singleton by name, a typed export, or a group registry.

Scene-wide find_child/find_children lookups are banned at runtime. They depend on node names and hierarchy and are slow. Use typed exports, groups (add_to_group/get_nodes_in_group on a known group) or a registry autoload.
String-name signal connections (Godot 3 style) are banned. Renames break silently. Connect the Signal object to a Callable: button.pressed.connect(_on_pressed).
Calling methods by string name is banned. Renames break silently and RPC targets become implicit. Use the method reference: _do_thing.call_deferred(), do_thing.rpc(), do_thing.rpc_id(peer_id).
OS.delay_msec/delay_usec block the main thread and freeze the game (and the server, in multiplayer). Use await get_tree().create_timer(seconds).timeout or a Timer node.

Writing Engine.time_scale is banned in networked games: peers' clocks drift and physics sync breaks. Pause with a server-side gate and one session clock. Remove this rule for single-player games (user approval).
Direct print calls are banned in gameplay code. Agents judge behavior from logs, so every line needs a category and level. Use the project's logger autoload (for example Log.info(category, message)).
